question: Intensive agriculture implies________.
option_2: cultivating large farms with moderately low inputs of labour and capital
option_3: use of more labour and capital inputs on the given land under cultivation
option_4: spreading farming across more states of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is use of more labour and capital inputs on the given land under cultivation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Intensive agriculture is a farming system characterised by high inputs of labour and capital relative to the land area used, aimed at maximising yield per unit of land. (गहन कृषि — अधिक श्रम और पूंजी)

 

• It relies on irrigation, high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, fertilisers and mechanisation to raise output from a limited landholding.

 

• It is commonly practised in densely populated regions with limited available land, such as parts of India, Japan and coastal China.

 

• It contrasts with extensive agriculture, where a large area of land is farmed with comparatively low input per unit area.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Intensive subsistence agriculture (rice-dominant) is common across South, Southeast and East Asia, driven by high population density and small landholdings.

 

• Extensive commercial agriculture is practised on large farms with low labour input per hectare in countries like the USA, Canada and Australia.

 

NOTE

 

• Bringing more land under cultivation (Option 1): Describes an expansion of cultivated area, characteristic of extensive rather than intensive agriculture.

 

• Cultivating large farms with moderately low inputs of labour and capital (Option 2): This is the definition of extensive agriculture, the opposite of intensive agriculture.

 

• Spreading farming across more states of India (Option 4): Unrelated to the technical definition of agricultural intensity.

question: Nana Sahib, a rebel at Kanpur was the son of which of the following Peshwas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Baji Rao II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nana Sahib (Dhondu Pant) was the adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao II, the last Peshwa of the Maratha Empire. (नाना साहेब — बाजी राव द्वितीय)

 

• He led the Revolt of 1857 at Kanpur (Cawnpore), one of the major centres of the uprising against the British.

 

• After Baji Rao II's death in 1851, the British East India Company, invoking the Doctrine of Lapse, refused to continue his pension to his adopted son Nana Sahib, fuelling his resentment against the Company.

 

• He was closely assisted by Tantia Tope during the Kanpur campaign against the British.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Baji Rao II (r. 1796-1818) was defeated by the British in the Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817-18), which ended the Maratha Empire; he was pensioned off to Bithoor, near Kanpur.

 

• Tantia Tope, Nana Sahib's general, was later captured and executed by the British in 1859.

 

NOTE

 

• Baji Rao I (Option 1): The Peshwa famed for expanding Maratha power in the early 18th century; unrelated to Nana Sahib of 1857.

 

• Balaji Baji Rao (Option 2): Son of Baji Rao I, Peshwa during the Third Battle of Panipat (1761); a different figure from the 1857 rebel Nana Sahib.

 

• Balaji Vishwanath (Option 4): The first Peshwa, appointed under Chhatrapati Shahu, and founder of the hereditary Peshwa lineage; unrelated to Nana Sahib.

question: Which of the following hill stations do NOT experience snowfall in winters?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ooty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ooty (Udhagamandalam), located in the Nilgiri Hills of Tamil Nadu, generally does not experience snowfall in winter. (ऊटी — बर्फबारी नहीं होती)

 

• Despite its elevation (about 2,240 m), Ooty's proximity to the equator keeps winter temperatures largely above freezing, so snowfall is essentially absent, unlike Himalayan hill stations.

 

• Nainital, Shimla and Srinagar, all located in the Himalayan region, regularly receive winter snowfall.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Nilgiri Hills, part of the Western Ghats, occasionally experience frost but not typical snowfall.

 

• Srinagar, in the Kashmir Valley, along with nearby Gulmarg, is renowned for heavy winter snowfall and skiing.

 

NOTE

 

• Nainital (Option 2): A hill station in Uttarakhand in the Himalayan foothills; receives occasional snowfall in winter.

 

• Shimla (Option 3): Capital of Himachal Pradesh and a well-known snowfall destination in winter.

 

• Srinagar (Option 4): Located in the Kashmir Valley; receives significant snowfall every winter.

question: Schools and hostels under the Ministry of Education's Samagra Shiksha scheme will be renamed after:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ministry of Education decided to rename over 1,000 residential schools and hostels funded under the Samagra Shiksha scheme as "Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose" residential schools/hostels. (नेताजी सुभाष चंद्र बोस — समग्र शिक्षा योजना)

 

• The decision was taken as a tribute marking Netaji's birth anniversary (23 January), observed as Parakram Diwas.

 

• Samagra Shiksha is an integrated scheme for school education, from pre-school to senior secondary level, launched in 2018 by merging the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan and Teacher Education schemes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan is administered by the Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education.

 

• 23 January is observed as "Parakram Diwas" to commemorate Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's birth anniversary.

 

NOTE

 

• Shyama Prasad Mukharjee (Option 1): Founder of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh; other schemes (e.g., the Rurban Mission) are named after him, not this one.

 

• Deen Dayal Upadhyaya (Option 3): Antyodaya and various rural welfare schemes are named after him, not the Samagra Shiksha hostels.

 

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (Option 4): The Statue of Unity and the "Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat" initiative are associated with him, not this renaming.

question: On 7 November 2022, Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended and offered prayers at celebrations of the ________ Prakash Parv of Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji at New Delhi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 553rd.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 7 November 2022, PM Narendra Modi attended and offered prayers at the 553rd Prakash Parv (birth anniversary celebrations) of Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji in New Delhi. (गुरु नानक देव जी — 553वां प्रकाश पर्व)

 

• Guru Nanak Dev Ji, founder of Sikhism, was born in 1469 at Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib); the year 2022 marks 553 years since his birth.

 

• The occasion is also known as Guru Purab or Gurpurab, celebrated on the full-moon day (Kartik Purnima) of the Kartik month.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guru Nanak Dev Ji was the first of the ten Sikh Gurus; the Guru Granth Sahib is the central scripture of Sikhism.

 

• Gurpurab celebrations typically include Akhand Path (continuous scripture reading), Nagar Kirtan processions and community langar.

 

NOTE

 

• 550th, 551st and 552nd (Options 1, 2 and 3): Each understates the number of years elapsed since Guru Nanak's birth in 1469, as counted in 2022; 553rd is the mathematically and factually correct figure.

question:
Match column A with column B.

Column A (Type of algae)      Column B (Proper Name)

a. Blue-green algae      i. Sargassum

b. Red algae      ii. Chlamydomonas

c. Green algae      iii. Rhodophyta

d. Brown algae      iv. Cyanobacteria
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct matching is: a. Blue-green algae – iv. Cyanobacteria; b. Red algae – iii. Rhodophyta; c. Green algae – ii. Chlamydomonas; d. Brown algae – i. Sargassum. (शैवाल वर्गीकरण — नील-हरित शैवाल = सायनोबैक्टीरिया)

 

• Blue-green algae (Cyanophyceae) are prokaryotic organisms commonly referred to as Cyanobacteria.

 

• Red algae belong to the phylum Rhodophyta, containing the pigment phycoerythrin that gives them their characteristic reddish colour; mostly marine.

 

• Green algae (Chlorophyceae) includes Chlamydomonas, a unicellular flagellate green alga widely studied in botany.

 

• Brown algae (Phaeophyceae) includes Sargassum, a large brown seaweed found in marine environments, notably the Sargasso Sea.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Algae are broadly classified based on pigmentation: Chlorophyceae (green; chlorophyll a and b), Phaeophyceae (brown; fucoxanthin), Rhodophyceae (red; phycoerythrin).

 

• Diatoms and dinoflagellates are other important algal groups, significant components of phytoplankton.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv): Mismatches all four pairs against the correct assignment.

 

• Option 2 (a-i, b-iii, c-ii, d-iv): Matches b and c correctly, but wrongly pairs a and d.

 

• Option 4 (a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i): Wrongly pairs a and b with c and d from the correct set; only c and d individually resemble correct types, but the combination is inconsistent with the correct matching.

question: What helps making the acidic food alkaline that is coming from the stomach?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bile juice.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bile juice, secreted by the liver and stored in the gallbladder, is alkaline and neutralises the acidic chyme entering the duodenum from the stomach. (पित्त रस — अम्लीय भोजन को क्षारीय बनाता है)

 

• It also emulsifies fats, breaking them into smaller globules to aid digestion by pancreatic lipase.

 

• Bile is released into the duodenum via the bile duct in response to the hormone cholecystokinin.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The liver is the largest gland in the human body and continuously produces bile; the gallbladder stores and concentrates it.

 

• Pancreatic juice, also alkaline, further helps neutralise stomach acid once food enters the small intestine.

 

NOTE

 

• Pepsin (Option 1): A stomach enzyme that digests proteins in an acidic environment; it does not neutralise acid.

 

• Gastric juice (Option 2): Itself acidic (contains hydrochloric acid), so it cannot make food alkaline.

 

• Hydrochloric acid (Option 3): The very acid secreted in the stomach that makes gastric contents acidic in the first place.

question: For which discovery did William Bradford Shockley, John Bardeen and Walter Houser Brattain jointly receive the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1956?
option_4: Discovery of receptors for temperature and touch
solution_text:
The correct answer is Discovery of transistor effect.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• William Shockley, John Bardeen and Walter Brattain jointly won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1956 "for their researches on semiconductors and their discovery of the transistor effect." (ट्रांजिस्टर प्रभाव — नोबेल भौतिकी पुरस्कार 1956)

 

• Their invention of the transistor at Bell Labs (1947) revolutionised electronics, replacing bulky vacuum tubes.

 

• The transistor effect refers to the ability of a small input signal to control a much larger output current/voltage through a semiconductor device.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bardeen went on to share a second Nobel Prize in Physics in 1972 (with Cooper and Schrieffer) for the theory of superconductivity, making him the only person to win the Physics Nobel twice.

 

• The transistor laid the foundation for modern integrated circuits and microprocessors.

 

NOTE

 

• Discovery of thermionic emission (Option 2): Associated with earlier vacuum-tube physics (e.g., the work of Owen Richardson, Nobel Prize 1928), not this trio's award.

 

• Discovery of electromagnetic induction (Option 3): Discovered by Michael Faraday in the 19th century; unrelated to this Nobel Prize.

 

• Discovery of receptors for temperature and touch (Option 4): This was the subject of the 2021 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (David Julius and Ardem Patapoutian), not the 1956 Physics prize.

question: Which group of rivers is a part of the peninsular drainage system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahanadi and Godavari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The peninsular drainage system of India comprises rivers originating on the peninsular plateau, and Mahanadi and Godavari are classic examples of such rivers. (प्रायद्वीपीय अपवाह तंत्र — महानदी और गोदावरी)

 

• These rivers are geologically older, flow over a stable landmass, follow rigid, structurally-controlled courses, and are largely rain-fed/non-perennial, unlike the Himalayan rivers.

 

• Godavari, the largest peninsular river, is called the "Dakshin Ganga"; Mahanadi flows through Chhattisgarh and Odisha into the Bay of Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major peninsular rivers include the Krishna, Cauvery, Narmada and Tapi.

 

• Narmada and Tapi are exceptions among peninsular rivers, as they flow west into the Arabian Sea through rift valleys, unlike most other peninsular rivers that flow east.

 

NOTE

 

• Gandak and Ghaghra (Option 1): Himalayan (extra-peninsular) rivers, tributaries of the Ganga, originating in the Himalayas.

 

• Ganga and Yamuna (Option 3): Major Himalayan rivers, part of the extra-peninsular/northern drainage system.

 

• Damodar and Sarda (Option 4): Damodar is a peninsular river, but Sarda (Kali/Sharda) is a Himalayan tributary of the Ghaghra, making this an inconsistent pairing for the peninsular system.

question: Ashoka sent a mission to spread the principle of Dhamma led by his son, Mahendra and daughter, Sanghamitra to ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ceylon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Emperor Ashoka sent his son Mahendra (Mahinda) and daughter Sanghamitra to Ceylon (present-day Sri Lanka) to spread Buddhism/Dhamma. (महेंद्र और संघमित्र — सीलोन/श्रीलंका)

 

• Mahendra converted the Sri Lankan king Devanampiya Tissa to Buddhism; Sanghamitra later carried a sapling of the original Bodhi Tree to Sri Lanka and established the order of Buddhist nuns there.

 

• This mission was part of Ashoka's wider dhamma-prachar (propagation of Buddhist principles) after the Kalinga War, with missionaries sent to regions within and outside India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ashoka's Rock Edict XIII records his remorse after the Kalinga War (261 BCE) and his subsequent embrace and propagation of Dhamma.

 

• The Mahavamsa and Dipavamsa, Sri Lankan chronicles, describe Mahendra's mission to the island in detail.

 

NOTE

 

• Kalinga (Option 1): The region Ashoka conquered in war, prompting his shift towards Dhamma — not the destination of Mahendra and Sanghamitra's mission.

 

• Cambodia (Option 3): Buddhism spread there later through separate trade and missionary contacts, not via this Ashokan mission.

 

• Thailand (Option 4): Also received Buddhism later through different channels, not through Mahendra and Sanghamitra.

question: If the government revenue expenditure exceeds revenue receipt, it is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is revenue deficit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A revenue deficit occurs when the government's revenue expenditure exceeds its revenue receipts. (राजस्व घाटा — राजस्व व्यय > राजस्व प्राप्ति)

 

• It indicates that the government is unable to meet its regular, day-to-day operational expenses from its regular income (tax and non-tax revenue).

 

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fiscal deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts excluding borrowings; it captures the government's total borrowing requirement.

 

• Primary deficit = Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments; it shows the deficit excluding the burden of past borrowings.

 

NOTE

 

• Primary deficit (Option 2): Fiscal deficit minus interest payments — a different concept from the revenue-versus-expenditure gap.

 

• Capital deficit (Option 3): Not a standard, formally defined fiscal indicator used in Indian budget documents for this concept.

 

• Fiscal deficit (Option 4): Relates to total expenditure exceeding total non-borrowed receipts, not specifically the revenue account.

question: Paramvir Chakra, Ashok Chakra and Vir Chakra are presented during the celebration of which day?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Republic Day.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gallantry awards including the Param Vir Chakra, Ashoka Chakra and Vir Chakra are announced/presented in connection with Republic Day celebrations (26 January) each year. (गणतंत्र दिवस — वीरता पुरस्कार)

 

• These are among India's highest military and peacetime gallantry awards, instituted to honour acts of exceptional valour.

 

• The Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime gallantry award; the Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime gallantry award, of equivalent stature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Republic Day parade at Kartavya Path, New Delhi, showcases India's military strength and cultural diversity, and gallantry awards are traditionally announced around this occasion.

 

• The Vir Chakra is the third-highest wartime gallantry award, after the Param Vir Chakra and Maha Vir Chakra.

 

NOTE

 

• Independence Day (Option 2): 15 August marks India's independence from British rule; the Prime Minister addresses the nation from the Red Fort, but this is not the specific occasion for these gallantry awards.

 

• Gandhi Jayanti (Option 3): 2 October commemorates Mahatma Gandhi's birthday; unrelated to these military awards.

 

• Indian Air Force Day (Option 4): 8 October celebrates the founding of the IAF; not specifically linked to the announcement of these awards.

question: The musician Sivamani is associated with which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Drums.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sivamani is a renowned Indian percussionist celebrated for his mastery of the drums, often blending them with various Indian and world percussion instruments. (शिवमणि — ड्रम वादक)

 

• He is known for his energetic live performances and fusion music, combining Western drum kits with Indian percussion styles.

 

• He has collaborated extensively with A. R. Rahman and performed at major national and international events.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sivamani has also experimented with unconventional percussion, including household objects, showcasing his versatility in rhythm.

 

• He has received several honours for his contribution to Indian music and percussion.

 

NOTE

 

• Violin (Option 2): Associated with artists like L. Subramaniam and M. S. Gopalakrishnan, not Sivamani's core instrument.

 

• Shehnai (Option 3): Famously associated with Ustad Bismillah Khan, not Sivamani.

 

• Sarod (Option 4): Associated with maestros like Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Amjad Ali Khan, not Sivamani.

question: Who among the following was the slave-general of Alauddin Khilji, who led his army in the battle against Ramachandra of Devagiri?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Malik Kafur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Malik Kafur was the slave-general of Sultan Alauddin Khilji who led the Khilji army in campaigns in the Deccan, including against Ramachandra (Ramchandra Dev) of Devagiri (the Yadava kingdom). (मलिक काफूर — अलाउद्दीन खिलजी का सेनापति)

 

• He led successive expeditions into the Deccan — Devagiri, Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai — between roughly 1308-1311, extending Khilji influence over southern India.

 

• After subduing Devagiri, Ramachandra was reinstated as a tributary ruler under the Delhi Sultanate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Malik Kafur later played a role in the succession crisis after Alauddin Khilji's death in 1316, briefly serving as regent before being killed.

 

• The Khilji dynasty's Deccan campaigns brought immense wealth to the Delhi Sultanate and expanded its southern frontier.

 

NOTE

 

• Nusrat Khan (Option 1): Another prominent general of Alauddin Khilji, associated with earlier campaigns such as Gujarat, not the Devagiri campaign against Ramachandra.

 

• Ulugh Khan (Option 3): A Khilji general/relative involved in the conquest of Gujarat and Ranthambore, not the Devagiri campaign in question.

 

• Zafar Khan (Option 4): A Khilji general known for the Ranthambore campaign, not associated with the Devagiri expedition against Ramachandra.

question: Padma Shri awardee in 2022, Arjun Singh Dhurve, is a tribal dancer of which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Baiga.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arjun Singh Dhurve, honoured with the Padma Shri in 2022, is a tribal dancer and singer associated with the Baiga dance form. (अर्जुन सिंह धुर्वे — बैगा नृत्य)

 

• He hails from Madhya Pradesh and has worked extensively to preserve and promote the folk traditions of the Baiga tribal community.

 

• The Padma Shri is India's fourth-highest civilian award, conferred for distinguished contributions in various fields, including art and folk culture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Baiga tribe is found primarily in Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, known for its distinct folk dance and traditional lifestyle.

 

• Several recent Padma awardees have been recognised specifically for grassroots preservation of tribal and folk art forms.

 

NOTE

 

• Chhau (Option 2): A semi-classical Indian dance form from Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal, unrelated to Arjun Singh Dhurve.

 

• Santhal (Option 3): Refers to a distinct tribal community and its own dance traditions, different from the Baiga dance associated with Dhurve.

 

• Tertali (Option 4): A folk dance from Rajasthan performed mainly by women of the Kamada community, unrelated to Dhurve.

question: क्रिकेट मैचों में मैदान में रहने वाले अंपायरों की संख्या ________ होती है। (In cricket matches, the number of umpires present on the field is ________.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a standard cricket match, two umpires are present on the field to officiate the game. (क्रिकेट मैच — मैदान में 2 अंपायर)

 

• One umpire stands at the bowler's end and the other at square leg, and they alternate ends after each over.

 

• In international matches, a third umpire (off-field, aided by technology for close decisions) and a match referee also assist, but only two umpires stand on the field itself.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The role of the third umpire has expanded with technology such as the Decision Review System (DRS), Hawk-Eye and UltraEdge.

 

• The Laws of Cricket are maintained and updated by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC).

 

NOTE

 

• 1, 3 and 4 (Options 1, 2 and 3): None of these match the standard number of on-field umpires, which is fixed at two under the Laws of Cricket.

question: Borgeet is associated with which Indian classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Borgeet (Bargeet) is a genre of devotional lyrical songs associated with the Sattriya dance form of Assam. (बरगीत — सत्रिया नृत्य)

 

• Both Borgeet and Sattriya dance were pioneered by the 15th-16th century Vaishnavite saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardeva as part of the Ekasarana Dharma tradition.

 

• Sattriya was recognised as one of India's classical dance forms by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000, traditionally performed in the sattras (Vaishnav monasteries) of Assam.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other works of Srimanta Sankardeva include Ankia Naat (one-act plays) and the Kirtana-Ghosha, a devotional text central to Assamese Vaishnavism.

 

• India officially recognises eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi and Sattriya.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi (Option 1): Classical dance of Odisha, associated with the worship of Lord Jagannath, not Borgeet.

 

• Manipuri (Option 2): Classical dance of Manipur, also rooted in Vaishnavism but distinct from the Assamese Borgeet/Sattriya tradition.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 4): Classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, unrelated to Borgeet.

question: 'BFSI' stands for Banking, Financial Services and ________ in India. It is a broad term for industries that offer financial products and services.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Insurance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• BFSI stands for Banking, Financial Services and Insurance, a broad term covering companies that provide a range of financial products and services. (बीएफएसआई — बैंकिंग, वित्तीय सेवाएं और बीमा)

 

• It encompasses commercial banks, insurance companies, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), mutual funds, cooperatives, and other financial intermediaries.

 

• The BFSI sector is one of the largest contributors to India's GDP and a major employment generator, especially in IT-enabled services.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulates the banking sector, while the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) regulates insurance.

 

• The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) regulates the securities/capital markets segment of BFSI.

 

NOTE

 

• Inflation (Option 1): An economic indicator of the general rise in prices, not part of the BFSI acronym.

 

• Investment (Option 2): Related to financial services broadly, but not the specific word represented by "I" in BFSI.

 

• Index Fund (Option 4): A specific type of investment vehicle, not the term denoted by "I" in BFSI.

question: What happens to the atomic size as you go down the group?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Increases.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As one moves down a group in the periodic table, the atomic size (atomic radius) increases. (परमाणु आकार — समूह में नीचे जाने पर बढ़ता है)

 

• This happens because each successive element down a group has an additional electron shell, increasing the distance between the nucleus and the outermost electrons.

 

• Although nuclear charge also increases down a group, the effect of the added electron shells (and increased shielding) dominates, resulting in a net increase in atomic radius.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Across a period (left to right), atomic size generally decreases due to increasing nuclear charge pulling electrons closer, with no new shell added.

 

• Ionisation energy generally decreases down a group as outer electrons are held less tightly due to increased atomic size.

 

NOTE

 

• Triples (Option 1): Not an accurate quantitative description; atomic radius increases gradually, not by a fixed multiple such as tripling.

 

• Decreases (Option 2): Contrary to the established periodic trend of atomic radius down a group.

 

• No change (Option 4): Incorrect, since the addition of new electron shells does change (increase) atomic size down a group.

question: The Fundamental Duties of citizens were added to the Constitution of India, upon the recommendations of which of the following committees?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swaran Singh Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution via the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. (मूल कर्तव्य — स्वर्ण सिंह समिति)

 

• The committee, headed by Sardar Swaran Singh, was constituted during the Emergency period to suggest constitutional amendments, including the incorporation of citizens' duties.

 

• Fundamental Duties are listed under Article 51A in Part IV-A of the Constitution; originally 10 duties were added, with an 11th added later.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The concept of Fundamental Duties was inspired partly by the model of the erstwhile USSR's Constitution.

 

• The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added the 11th Fundamental Duty, relating to parents/guardians providing opportunities for education to children aged 6-14 years.

 

NOTE

 

• Raja Chelliah Committee (Option 1): Associated with tax reforms in India, not Fundamental Duties.

 

• Santhanam Committee (Option 2): Related to the prevention of corruption, leading to the establishment of the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC), not Fundamental Duties.

 

• Kelkar Committee (Option 3): Associated with tax reforms and infrastructure financing, not Fundamental Duties.

question: Who was behind publishing the first News Paper in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is James Augustus Hickey.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• James Augustus Hickey was behind publishing the first newspaper in India, the "Bengal Gazette" (also called "Hicky's Bengal Gazette" or the "Calcutta General Advertiser"), started in 1780. (जेम्स ऑगस्टस हिक्की — भारत का पहला समाचार पत्र)

 

• It was a weekly English-language newspaper published from Calcutta, known for its critical coverage of the East India Company's administration, including Governor-General Warren Hastings.

 

• Hickey was eventually imprisoned and his press seized due to his outspoken criticism of Company officials.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hicky's Bengal Gazette is regarded as the beginning of the newspaper/press tradition in India.

 

• Among the notable early vernacular newspapers was the "Samachar Darpan" (1818), published in Bengali.

 

NOTE

 

• Deen Bandhu Mitra (Option 1): A Bengali playwright and writer, known for works like "Nil Darpan", not associated with founding a newspaper in this context.

 

• Hem Chandrakar (Option 3): Not associated with founding India's first newspaper.

 

• Harishchandra Mukherjee (Option 4): Editor of "The Hindoo Patriot," an important later 19th-century newspaper, not India's first newspaper.

question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Centre-State Relations pertaining to the three lists of the Indian Constitution?

A.The subjects which are not included in any of the three lists are called Residuary subjects.

B.If there is any conflict between the Union List and the State List, then the former prevails.

C.When the Parliament enacts a law on the request of two or more states, then that law made by the Parliament on the State List is applicable to all the states.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A and B only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statements A and B are correct, while statement C is incorrect. (केंद्र-राज्य संबंध — अवशिष्ट विषय और संघ सूची की प्रधानता)

 

• Statement A is correct: Under Article 248, the residuary power of legislation — subjects not enumerated in the Union, State or Concurrent Lists — rests with Parliament; such subjects are called Residuary subjects.

 

• Statement B is correct: Under Article 246, in case of any conflict regarding legislative competence between the Union List and the State List, the Union List (Parliament's power) prevails, given the non-obstante clause "notwithstanding anything in clauses (2) and (3)."

 

• Statement C is incorrect: Under Article 252, when two or more states pass resolutions requesting Parliament to legislate on a State List subject, the resulting law applies only to the consenting states (other states may later adopt it by passing a similar resolution) — it does not automatically become applicable to all states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 254 deals with repugnancy between laws made by Parliament and laws made by state legislatures on Concurrent List subjects — the Union law prevails in case of conflict, subject to the President's assent for the state law.

 

• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution divides subjects among the Union List (List I), State List (List II) and Concurrent List (List III).

 

NOTE

 

• A and C only (Option 1), B and C only (Option 2) and A, B and C (Option 3): All three incorrectly include statement C, which wrongly asserts that a law made under Article 252 automatically applies to all states.

question: What is the child sex ratio in India in the 2011 Census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 914 females per 1000 males.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The child sex ratio (0-6 years) in India as per the 2011 Census was 914 females per 1000 males. (बाल लिंगानुपात 2011 — 914)

 

• This was a decline compared to the child sex ratio of 927 recorded in the 2001 Census, indicating a worsening trend in the 0-6 age group despite the overall sex ratio improving.

 

• The overall sex ratio for India in the 2011 Census was 943 females per 1000 males, an improvement from 933 in 2001.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala recorded among the best sex ratios among Indian states in 2011, while Haryana recorded one of the worst child sex ratios.

 

• The "Beti Bachao Beti Padhao" scheme, launched in 2015, aims to address the declining child sex ratio and promote girls' education.

 

NOTE

 

• 911 females per 1000 males (Option 2): A close but incorrect figure, not matching the officially recorded 2011 Census child sex ratio.

 

• 941 females per 1000 males (Option 3): Does not match the recorded child sex ratio figure for 2011.

 

• 814 females per 1000 males (Option 4): Significantly understates the actual 2011 child sex ratio figure.
